died1: ^Once upon a time, there lived a Greek hero.

^This hero met a great sage, who, out of the kindness of his heart, offered him selfless help. The sage promised to make him the greatest of the great — to drink fine wine and wipe his mouth with golden napkins...
^Tempted by such an offer, the hero agreed, and they began his training.

^Time passed, and just as the sage had promised, the hero grew stronger and more powerful. But then, an unexpected figure appeared — one who tempted him with fleeting pleasures and hollow victories. Slowly, our hero forgot his real goal and became addicted to the taste for those short-lived triumphs that gave only an illusion of success...
^And eventually, he lost his mind — forgot his purpose, his achievements. His great mentor, the sage, turned away from him, and the hero became no one but a madman. Guess what his name was?
^Not true! You never offered me golden napkins or wine!
^If I did, would you stop participating in Dionysus’ foolish lottery?
^Then prepare to lose your mind, oh greatest of fools!
^I’m ready for such sacrifices, oh my great and wise mentor!
died2: ^Why so quiet? Swallow a fish? I thought that was my role, or did our dynamic change while I wasn’t looking?
^Everything’s the same… I’m just a wise goddess trying to win with a foolish little fish.
^Glad to hear that. Some things never change!
^I’d prefer if that “never changing” started moving toward, let's say, a victory. Any thoughts?
^Apistos! Are you joking?! Victory in the tournament!
^Pffhahaha! Oh, I remember, don’t worry. I’ll bring you that win, milady. Really.
^It would be nice if that were true…
